questions.q: Engineers need an interactive shell on EC2 instances in private subnets. Security forbids inbound ports, bastion hosts and SSH keys, and wants an IAM-based audit trail. Which solution fits?

options.t: A bastion host with SSH key pairs
options.why: Wrong: it needs an inbound port and key management.
Right: access goes through IAM (`ssm:StartSession`), needs no inbound ports or keys, and sessions are logged to S3 or CloudWatch Logs.

options.t: Open port 22 to the corporate CIDR in the security group
options.why: Wrong: it still opens an inbound port and relies on keys.
Wrong: it runs scripts, not an interactive shell.

questions.explain: Session Manager gives shell access with no inbound ports, bastion or keys.
questions.remember: No-SSH, no-bastion, no-inbound-port shell access with audit → Session Manager, logged to S3 or CloudWatch Logs.
variants: Run one script on many nodes at once → Run Command.
Reach a private RDS or Redshift from a laptop → Session Manager port forwarding to a remote host.
SSH/RDP to private instances without an agent → EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint.

questions.q: A developer must reach a private Redshift cluster from a laptop. No inbound security group rules may be added. A managed EC2 instance already runs in the same VPC. What should they use?

options.t: Session Manager port forwarding to the remote host through the EC2 instance
options.why: Right: the `AWS-StartPortForwardingSessionToRemoteHost` document tunnels to a private host and port with no inbound ports.

options.t: Run Command to start a database client on the instance
options.why: Wrong: it runs commands on the node and does not create a tunnel to the laptop.
Wrong: it browses node files and does not forward database ports.
Wrong: it enforces desired state on a schedule and gives no network access.

questions.explain: Port forwarding to a remote host reaches private databases through a managed node.
questions.remember: Tunnel to a private database with no inbound ports → Session Manager port forwarding to remote host via a managed node.
variants: Interactive shell on the node itself → Session Manager standard session.
Many nodes need the same script → Run Command.
A node that is not managed cannot be used as a jump host → fix agent, IAM role and endpoints first.

questions.q: An EC2 instance in a private subnet with no NAT does not appear in Systems Manager. Which TWO checks address the most likely causes?

options.t: Confirm the instance profile (or Default Host Management Configuration) grants `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` permissions
options.why: Right: a managed node needs IAM permission.

options.t: Confirm interface VPC endpoints exist for `ssm`, `ssmmessages` and `ec2messages`
options.why: Right: the agent needs an outbound HTTPS path to those endpoints; without NAT, endpoints provide it.
Wrong: SSM needs no inbound ports; the agent connects outbound.

options.t: Create a Resource Data Sync to S3
options.why: Wrong: it exports inventory and does not make a node managed.
Wrong: it blocks or allows actions on dates and does not affect registration.

questions.explain: The three prerequisites are agent, IAM permission and a network path to SSM.
questions.remember: Node not managed → check SSM Agent, instance profile or DHMC, and endpoints (or NAT) to ssm, ssmmessages, ec2messages.
variants: Node is a hybrid server → it needs a hybrid activation and gets an `mi-` ID.
Wrong Region or stopped instance → also makes it unlisted.
Agent not installed on a custom AMI → install the SSM Agent.

questions.q: AWS Config flags S3 buckets without default encryption. The company wants the fix applied automatically with least operational effort. What should it use?

options.t: A Config remediation action that runs a Systems Manager Automation runbook
options.why: Right: Automation applies the fix, and AWS-owned runbooks such as `AWS-EnableS3BucketEncryption` exist.

options.t: A Run Command document on every bucket
options.why: Wrong: Run Command targets nodes, not S3 buckets.
Wrong: it patches operating systems, not bucket settings.

options.t: A Session Manager session to each bucket
options.why: Wrong: sessions give shell access to nodes, not bucket access.

questions.explain: Config auto remediation uses SSM Automation runbooks.
questions.remember: A Config rule needs an automatic fix → Config remediation with an SSM Automation runbook.
variants: Block public access on S3 → `AWS-ConfigureS3BucketPublicAccessBlock` runbook.
Remediate on a non-Config event → EventBridge rule that starts an Automation.
Fix must wait for a human OK → add an `aws:approve` step.

questions.q: A runbook deletes old data and a manager must approve before the delete step runs. Which Automation feature provides this?

options.t: The `aws:approve` action, which pauses and notifies through SNS
options.why: Right: it adds a human approval step in the workflow.
Wrong: it only waits for a fixed time.
Wrong: it branches on conditions and does not ask a human.
Wrong: it re-applies desired state and does not pause for approval.

questions.explain: `aws:approve` gives human-in-the-loop approval inside a runbook.
questions.remember: Runbook needs manager approval → `aws:approve` step with SNS.
variants: Wait for a resource property → `aws:waitForAwsResourceProperty`.
Run a Python script step → `aws:executeScript`.
Block changes on freeze dates → Change Calendar.

questions.q: A team must patch 500 Linux instances monthly during an approved window and report compliance. Which design fits?

options.t: Patch Manager with a custom patch baseline, patch groups, and a maintenance window
options.why: Right: baselines define approved patches, tags map nodes to them, the window schedules the patching, and compliance is reported.

options.t: Manual SSH sessions to each instance
options.why: Wrong: it does not scale and gives no compliance reporting.

options.t: Rely on the default patch baseline and Patch Manager rollback
options.why: Wrong: Patch Manager has no automatic rollback; use AMI snapshots or blue-green.
Wrong: it collects metadata and does not install patches.

questions.explain: Patch Manager plus baseline plus maintenance window (or patch policy) is the standard pattern.
questions.remember: Fleet patching on a schedule with compliance → Patch Manager with baseline and maintenance window or patch policy.
variants: Org-wide patching across accounts and Regions → patch policy via Quick Setup.
EMR or container hosts → replace AMIs or images, not in-place patching.
Need rollback → use AMI snapshots or blue-green, since it is not automatic.

questions.q: Compliance requires the CloudWatch agent to stay installed on all nodes tagged `env=prod`. If someone removes it, it must be restored on a schedule. Which feature fits?

options.why: Right: it applies a document to tagged targets on a schedule and re-applies the desired state.
Wrong: it executes once and does not enforce state over time.
Wrong: it handles incident response, not configuration enforcement.
Wrong: it only provides a schedule; the enforcement comes from associations.

questions.explain: State Manager enforces desired state through associations.
questions.remember: Keep something installed or configured over time → State Manager association; one-off ad-hoc command → Run Command.
variants: Run a command on `role=kafka` nodes with a failure limit → Run Command with concurrency and error thresholds.
Keep the SSM Agent updated → association with `AWS-UpdateSSMAgent`.
Org-wide baseline setup → Quick Setup.

questions.q: A critical CloudWatch alarm must page the on-call engineer, escalate if there is no response, and keep a timeline for post-incident review. Which service?

options.t: Systems Manager Incident Manager with a response plan
options.why: Right: it engages contacts, escalates, tracks a timeline and supports post-incident analysis.
Wrong: it tracks OpsItems for resolution but is not built for on-call engagement and escalation.
Wrong: it manages approved changes, not alarms.
Wrong: it distributes software packages.

questions.explain: Incident Manager is the on-call, escalation and timeline tool.
questions.remember: Alarm needs paging, escalation and a post-incident review → Incident Manager response plan.
variants: Alarm should just create a trackable ticket with runbooks → CloudWatch alarm to OpsCenter OpsItem.
Production change needs approvals → Change Manager with Change Calendar.
Aggregated ops dashboard across accounts → Explorer.

questions.q: Alarms and Security Hub findings should open operational issues that engineers investigate and resolve with attached Automation runbooks, without paging anyone. Which feature?

options.why: Right: OpsItems are created automatically from alarms, EventBridge, Security Hub and Config, and runbooks can be attached to resolve them.
Wrong: it focuses on engagement and escalation for critical incidents.
Wrong: it is a GUI for managing nodes.
Wrong: it enforces configuration on nodes.

questions.explain: OpsCenter is the central place to view and resolve OpsItems.
questions.remember: Centralize and resolve operational issues with runbooks → OpsCenter; page and escalate → Incident Manager.
variants: Dashboard of OpsData across accounts → Explorer.
Many OpsItems flood in → tune and deduplicate sources.
Approvals for changes → Change Manager.

questions.q: A team needs a fleet software inventory they can query with Athena, including data from several accounts. Which design fits?

options.t: Systems Manager Inventory with Resource Data Sync to S3
options.why: Right: Resource Data Sync exports inventory as JSON to S3, across accounts and Regions, so Athena can query it.

options.t: Run Command output in the console
options.why: Wrong: console output is limited and not queryable at scale.
Wrong: they record shell sessions, not installed software.
Wrong: it reports missing patches, not a full software inventory.

questions.explain: Inventory plus Resource Data Sync to S3 makes fleet metadata queryable.
questions.remember: Fleet metadata queryable in Athena or QuickSight → Inventory with Resource Data Sync to S3.
variants: Inventory missing → check the association and the S3 bucket policy for the sync.
Pipeline config or secrets as parameters → Parameter Store `SecureString`.
Patch compliance export → also through Resource Data Sync.
